t: Listen to a talk in a business class.
When a company launches a new product, how should it set the price?
With penetration pricing, a company starts with a low price.
The goal is to attract a lot of customers quickly and win market share.
Later, once people are loyal, the price can go up.
The company starts with a high price, aimed at early adopters who are willing to pay more to have the product first, and then lowers the price over time.
New smartphones are a good example.
They're most expensive in the first few months.
Finally, value-based pricing ignores production costs and competitors' prices.
Instead, the price is based on how much customers believe the product is worth to them.
So: start low, start high, or price by perceived value.
